greek_erechtheus.name: Repel the invader through the sacrifice of his daughters
greek_erechtheus.notes: To win the Eleusinian war against Eumolpus and the Thracians, Erechtheus offered up his own daughters as the oracle demanded, securing victory and the death of Eumolpus before Poseidon destroyed him with a thunderbolt (or trident).

greek_erechtheus.name: Persist after death as the earth-shaking Poseidon Erechtheus
greek_erechtheus.notes: Absorbed into the cult of Poseidon on the Athenian Acropolis as the syncretic Poseidon Erechtheus, sharing the trident and the salt sea of the Erechtheion.

greek_eumelus.name: Peerless chariot-driving with the swiftest mares
greek_eumelus.notes: Homer names Eumelus's Apollo-reared mares the best horses at Troy and Eumelus himself the best charioteer; he led the funeral-games race for Patroclus and would have won but for a divinely broken yoke (Athena aiding Diomedes).

greek_europa.name: Bear the three judge-kings of Crete to Zeus
greek_europa.notes: By Zeus she bore Minos, Rhadamanthys and Sarpedon, founders of Cretan kingship and (Minos and Rhadamanthys) judges of the dead.

sources.reference: Hesiod, Catalogue of Women fr. 140; Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 3.1.1

greek_eurynome.name: Bear Bellerophon, the Chimera-slayer, to Poseidon
greek_eurynome.notes: Wife of Glaucus of Corinth but mother of the hero Bellerophon by Poseidon; Hesiod praises her as endowed by Athena with beauty and wisdom.

sources.reference: Hesiod, Catalogue of Women fr. 43a; Homer, Iliad 6.155-159

greek_ganymede.name: Pour the nectar of the gods on Olympus
greek_ganymede.notes: Made wine-pourer (oinochoos) to Zeus and the Olympians in place of Hebe, drawing nectar from the mixing-bowl.

sources.reference: Homer, Iliad 20.232-235; Homeric Hymn to Aphrodite 202-217

greek_harmonia.name: Bind together in harmony and marital concord
greek_harmonia.notes: Personified Harmony, the joining of opposites into accord; her wedding to Cadmus, attended by all the gods, was the mythic archetype of divinely-sanctioned marriage.

greek_hecuba.name: Exact blinding vengeance on the murderer of her child
greek_hecuba.notes: With the captive Trojan women she lured Polymestor into her tent and gouged out his eyes with brooch-pins, killing his sons, in requital for his murder of Polydorus.

greek_hecuba.name: Transform at death into a fiery-eyed hound
greek_hecuba.notes: Polymestor's prophecy and later tradition make her end a metamorphosis into a bitch with blazing eyes, buried at Cynossema ('the bitch's tomb'), a Hellespontine landmark for sailors.

greek_helen.name: Surpassing beauty that compels and ruins men
greek_helen.notes: The most beautiful of mortal women, whose face moved all Greece to war; the Trojan elders judge her beauty 'terribly like the immortal goddesses' even as they wish her gone.

greek_helen.name: Knowledge of Egyptian grief-banishing drugs
greek_helen.notes: In the Odyssey she casts into the wine the drug nepenthes, given her by Polydamna of Egypt, that quiets all pain and anger.

greek_helenus.name: True augury and the bird-borne knowledge of fate
greek_helenus.notes: Foremost augur of Troy, 'best of bird-seers'; his prophecy, extracted after his capture by Odysseus, named the conditions for Troy's fall (the bow of Heracles, Neoptolemus, the Palladium).

greek_hesiod_atlas.name: Knowledge of the depths of the whole sea and the heavens
greek_hesiod_atlas.notes: Homer calls him the Titan who 'knows the depths of every sea' and guards the pillars that keep earth and sky apart; later he is the astronomer-king who first taught the sphere.

greek_hesiod_clio.name: Proclaim and immortalize renown in song
greek_hesiod_clio.notes: Her name from kleos ('fame, glory'); she makes famous and is herself the Muse who celebrates the deeds of heroes, later differentiated as the Muse of history.

greek_hesiod_epimetheus.name: Afterthought: act and only then perceive consequence
greek_hesiod_epimetheus.notes: The 'after-thinker' who, against Prometheus's warning, accepted Pandora from the gods and so loosed evils on mankind; his very nature is to learn too late.

sources.reference: Scholia and tradition of the Eumolpidae; cf. Apollodorus 3.15.4

greek_eumolpus.name: Aulos and lyre of the fair singer

sources.reference: Attic vase iconography; cf. Pindar, Olympian 1.43-45

greek_helenus.name: Augur's staff (the lituus/skeptron of the seer)

sources.reference: Virgil, Aeneid 3.358-373 (Helenus as priest-king of Buthrotum)
Homeric Hymn 31 to Helios 9-15; Rhodian coinage

greek_hesiod_helios.name: The sacred cattle of the Sun

greek_hesiod_hera.name: Polos / stephane crown of the queen

sources.reference: Pausanias 2.17.4 (Polyclitus's chryselephantine Hera at the Argive Heraion)

greek_hesiod_hestia.name: The sacred hearth and undying fire

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn 24 to Hestia; Homeric Hymn 29 to Hestia 1-6
Roman-era Muse iconography; cf. Hesiod, Theogony 79-80
Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 3.1.1 (mother of the Cretan kings)
Homer, Iliad 2.711-715 (leader of the Pherae contingent)
Homeric Hymn to Demeter 473-482 (Demeter instructs Eumolpus in the rites)

greek_europa.gloss: the cult-title of Europa at the Hellotia of Gortyn/Corinth

sources.reference: Hesiod, Theogony 454; Homeric Hymn 5 to Aphrodite 22
Hesiod, Works and Days 111-120 (the golden race under Cronus)

greek_erechtheus.name: Joint cult of Poseidon Erechtheus on the Acropolis
greek_erechtheus.notes: Worshipped in the Erechtheion beside Athena Polias, with the priest of Poseidon Erechtheus among the chief Athenian priesthoods; the salt 'sea' (thalassa) and trident-marks in the rock belonged to his sanctuary.

greek_europa.name: Hellotia festival at Gortyn
greek_europa.notes: The Cretans of Gortyn honoured Europa as Hellotis with the Hellotia, in which an enormous myrtle wreath was carried in procession, said to contain the bones of Europa; the rite had an initiatory aspect for young men.

greek_eumolpus.name: Eleusinian Mysteries as founding hierophant
greek_eumolpus.notes: Reckoned the first hierophant and eponymous ancestor of the Eumolpidae, the hereditary clan that supplied the hierophant of the Eleusinian Mysteries for a millennium; his tomb stood at Eleusis.

greek_helen.name: Cult of Helen at the Platanistas and the Menelaion
greek_helen.notes: Worshipped as a goddess at Sparta: at the urban Platanistas (the plane-grove) where girls sang her epithalamia, and shared a shrine with Menelaus and the Dioscuri at the Menelaion at Therapne. On Rhodes she was Helen Dendritis, hung from a tree by Polyxo's pretended Furies.

greek_hesiod_cronus.name: Kronia harvest festival at Athens
greek_hesiod_cronus.notes: Held on Hekatombaion 12 to mark the first harvest; masters and slaves feasted together in a remembrance of the egalitarian Golden Age under Cronus's rule. A precinct of Cronus and Rhea stood at Athens.

greek_hesiod_helios.name: Halieia of Rhodes with the chariot-into-sea sacrifice
greek_hesiod_helios.notes: On Rhodes, where Helios was patron and the Colossus stood, the Halieia featured athletic, equestrian and musical contests and the annual drowning of a four-horse chariot in the sea as an image of the sinking sun.

sources.reference: Pindar, Olympian 7.54-76; Festus, De verborum significatu s.v. October equus (comparandum)

greek_hesiod_hephaestus.name: Chalkeia of the Athenian smiths
greek_hesiod_hephaestus.notes: On the last day of Pyanepsion, craftsmen and especially bronze-smiths processed in honour of Hephaestus together with Athena Ergane; the Hephaisteia at Athens and the quadrennial torch-race festival on Lemnos were his other principal rites.

sources.reference: Harpocration and Suda s.v. Chalkeia; Pausanias 1.30.2

greek_hesiod_hermes.name: Worship at herms and the gymnasium Hermaia
greek_hesiod_hermes.notes: Honoured at the herms (square pillars with his head and phallus) set at crossroads, doorways and boundaries with libations of wine and honey; the Hermaia in the gymnasia celebrated him as patron of youths and athletes, with hierarchies temporarily inverted.

greek_hesiod_hades.name: Annual opening of the temple of Hades at Elis
greek_hesiod_hades.notes: Pausanias reports that the Eleans alone worshipped Hades, opening his sacred enclosure once each year, when only the priest might enter; elsewhere he received black victims in nocturnal chthonic rites.

greek_hesiod_boreas.name: Boreas cult on the Ilissus and the Thurian thank-offering
greek_hesiod_boreas.notes: After his storm wrecked the Persian fleet off Sepias, the Athenians built him a sanctuary on the Ilissus; the Thurians sacrificed to him yearly as Euergetes ('Benefactor') for destroying the fleet of Dionysius. Destructive winds received black victims.

greek_hesiod_calliope.name: Cult of the Muses on Helicon (Mouseia at Thespiae)
greek_hesiod_calliope.notes: The Muses, born in Pieria, were worshipped chiefly in the grove of the Helicon above Thespiae, where the Thespians held the quadrennial Mouseia with musical and poetic contests by the Hippocrene spring.

attributes.name: Maiden riding the bull over the sea
attributes.notes: The dominant image, fixed on Cretan (especially Gortynian) coinage: Europa seated side-saddle on the swimming bull, her veil or mantle billowing in an arc above her.

sources.reference: Moschus, Europa; Gortynian coinage 5th c. BCE - 2nd c. CE
Gortynian silver staters showing Europa in the plane-tree with the eagle

sacredPlants.name: Plane tree of Gortyn (evergreen, sacred to the union)

sources.reference: Theophrastus, Historia Plantarum 1.9.5; Pliny, Natural History 12.11

attributes.name: Wine-cup and jug of the cupbearer
attributes.notes: Shown as a beautiful youth, often in a Phrygian cap, holding the cup and oinochoe with which he serves the gods; the abduction scene shows the eagle bearing him aloft.

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn to Aphrodite 202-217; Attic vase iconography

sacredAnimals.name: Eagle of Zeus (his abductor; constellation Aquila)

attributes.name: The necklace and robe of Harmonia
attributes.notes: Recognized by Hephaestus's golden necklace wrought as two intertwined serpents, and by the woven peplos given at her wedding; both objects cursed to ruin the house of Cadmus.

sacredAnimals.name: Serpent (she and Cadmus transformed into snakes in old age)

attributes.name: Bronze helmet with nodding horsehair crest
attributes.notes: His signature image, the flashing crested helm of korythaiolos Hektor, whose nodding plume frightens the infant Astyanax at the Scaean Gate in Iliad 6.

attributes.name: The egg of Leda from which she was born
attributes.notes: Her Spartan birth-token: she hatched from an egg laid by Leda after Zeus's visitation as a swan; the egg was shown hanging in the temple of the Leukippides at Sparta.

sacredPlants.name: Plane tree (the Platanistas grove; 'Helen's tree' on Rhodes)

attributes.name: Saffron robe and rosy fingers in a winged figure
attributes.notes: Depicted as a winged goddess in a saffron mantle (krokopeplos), rosy-fingered, rising from Ocean to open heaven's gates before the chariot of the Sun.

attributes.name: Radiate crown and the all-seeing eye
attributes.notes: Crowned with a wreath of sun-rays, driving a four-horse chariot across the sky; the god 'who sees all and hears all', invoked as witness of oaths.

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn 31 to Helios 9-16; Homer, Iliad 3.277

sacredAnimals.name: White horses of the solar chariot

attributes.name: Triple-bodied form at the crossroads (hekataion)
attributes.notes: From the late 5th c. BCE (Alcamenes' Hekate Epipyrgidia on the Athenian Acropolis) shown three-formed about a central pillar, holding paired torches, and often keys, daggers or serpents.

sacredAnimals.name: Peacock (its tail bearing the eyes of Argos)

sources.reference: Homer, Iliad 1.551 and passim (boopis potnia Here)

sacredAnimals.name: Cuckoo (Zeus's seductive disguise; perched on her sceptre)

sacredPlants.name: Pomegranate (emblem of marriage and fecundity, held in her cult-statue)

sacredAnimals.name: Tortoise (from whose shell he made the first lyre)
Ram (Kriophoros, the ram-bearer who saved Tanagra from plague)

attributes.name: Craftsman's cap (pilos), hammer and tongs
attributes.notes: Shown as a bearded smith in the conical workman's cap and short chiton, hammer and tongs in hand, often lame-footed at his forge.

sacredAnimals.name: Donkey (his mount in the return-to-Olympus procession)

sources.reference: Attic vase iconography of the Return of Hephaestus; cf. Pausanias 1.20.3

attributes.name: Jagged sickle (harpe) and veiled head
attributes.notes: Identified by the adamantine harpe with which he castrated Uranus, a tool also read as the sickle of the harvest; often shown with a veiled or covered head.

attributes.name: Bearing the vault of heaven on neck and hands
attributes.notes: Standing at the western edge of the world, straining to hold the broad sky apart from earth; the celestial globe is later substituted for the sky in Hellenistic and Roman art.

sacredAnimals.name: Pig (sacrificed at the Thesmophoria; emblem of fertility)

sources.reference: Scholia to Lucian, Dialogues of the Courtesans 2.1 (the Thesmophoria megara)
Homeric Hymn to Demeter; Ovid, Metamorphoses 5.642-647

sacredPlants.name: Poppy and grain (the gephyra of cereal and the sleep-poppy)

sources.reference: Theocritus, Idyll 7.155-157; Callimachus, Hymn 6 to Demeter

sacredPlants.name: Mint (minthe, used in the kykeon of Eleusis)

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn to Demeter 208-209; Ovid, Metamorphoses 10.728-731

attributes.name: Veiled, fully-draped seated goddess by the hearth
attributes.notes: Shown as a modestly veiled woman, never nude, seated or standing in long robes, sometimes holding a flowering branch; her aniconic presence is the hearth-fire itself.

sources.reference: Athenian vase iconography; cf. Homeric Hymn 29 to Hestia

attributes.name: Hierophant's sceptre and ceremonial robe
attributes.notes: Imagined in the dress of the hierophant whose role he founded: long sacral robe, fillet, and sceptre, his 'fair voice' chanting the sacred formulae of the Mysteries.

sources.reference: Tradition of the Eumolpidae; cf. Pausanias 1.38.3
